stem: What is a **population**?

options.content: A group of organisms of one species, living in the same area, at the same time
options.rationale: For example, all the impala in Hwange this year.

options.content: All the different species living in an area
options.rationale: That is a community.

options.content: All the organisms living in an area together with their whole physical environment
options.rationale: That is an ecosystem.

options.content: The number of people living in a country
options.rationale: In biology, a population can be of any species.

explanation: A population is a group of organisms of one species living in the same area at the same time.
hints: How many species are in a population?

stem: What is a **community**?

options.content: A group of organisms of one species in one area
options.rationale: That is a population.

options.content: The physical surroundings of an organism, such as soil and water
options.rationale: That is part of the environment.

options.content: All of the populations of different species in an ecosystem
options.rationale: A community includes every species present.

options.content: A group of animals that live in a herd
options.rationale: A herd is part of one population.

explanation: A community is all the populations of different species in an ecosystem, such as all the plants, animals and microorganisms of a vlei.
hints: A community has many species.

stem: True or false: in the stationary phase of a sigmoid growth curve, the birth rate is equal to the death rate.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. Births and deaths balance, so the population stays roughly constant.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true. In the stationary phase individuals are still born and still die, but at equal rates, so the numbers stay level.

explanation: In the stationary phase limiting factors such as food shortage and waste build-up slow reproduction and increase deaths until the birth rate equals the death rate, so the population stays roughly constant.
hints: Why does the curve level off?

stem: Name the phase of a sigmoid population growth curve in which the population increases most rapidly.

rejected.feedback: In the lag phase numbers increase slowly. The fastest increase is in the exponential (log) phase.
In the stationary phase numbers stay constant.
In the death phase numbers fall.

explanation: In the exponential (log) phase there is plenty of food and space, so the birth rate far exceeds the death rate and the population doubles at regular intervals.
hints: The population doubles again and again.

stem: Which of these is an **ecosystem**?

options.content: All the impala in Hwange National Park
options.rationale: That is a population of one species.

options.content: All the plants and animals living together in a vlei
options.rationale: Without the physical environment, this is a community.

options.content: The water, soil and rocks of a river bank and its bed
options.rationale: These are only the non-living parts of an environment.

options.content: Lake Kariba, with its organisms and the water, mud and air
options.rationale: An ecosystem is the community plus its environment.

explanation: An ecosystem is a unit containing the community of organisms and their environment, interacting together, such as a lake, a vlei or a rotting log.
hints: An ecosystem includes living and non-living parts.

stem: Match each phase of a sigmoid growth curve with what happens to the population.

right.content: Numbers increase slowly as the organisms adjust and begin to reproduce
Numbers increase rapidly, doubling at regular intervals
Numbers stay roughly constant because the birth rate equals the death rate
Numbers fall because the death rate is greater than the birth rate
Numbers rise and fall at random with no pattern

explanation: Lag: slow increase. Exponential: rapid doubling. Stationary: births equal deaths. Death: deaths exceed births.
hints: Picture the S-shaped curve from left to right.

stem: Each sentence describes a factor that affects population size in Hwange. Choose the correct factor for each.

payload.template: Lions killing impala is an example of {{blank:pred}}. Impala and zebra eating the same grass is an example of {{blank:comp}}. An outbreak of anthrax that kills many animals is an example of {{blank:dis}}. A drought that reduces the growth of grass reduces the {{blank:food}} supply.

explanation: Predation (lions killing impala), competition (two species sharing grass), disease (anthrax) and food supply (reduced by drought) all affect the rate of population growth.
hints: Predators kill; competitors share a limited resource.

stem: A culture begins with 200 bacteria. Each bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes. Assuming no bacteria die, how many will there be after 2 hours?
explanation: 2 hours = 120 minutes, which allows $120 \div 20 = 6$ divisions. The population doubles each time: $200 \times 2^6 = 200 \times 64 = 12\,800$.
workedSolution:
1. Number of divisions $= \dfrac{120\ \text{min}}{20\ \text{min}} = 6$.
2. Number of bacteria $= 200 \times 2^6 = 200 \times 64 = 12\,800$.
hints: How many times does the population double in 2 hours?

stem: Yeast is added to a flask of sugar solution. Why does the yeast population grow only slowly at first (the lag phase)?

options.content: Because the sugar has already run out
options.rationale: At the start there is plenty of sugar.

options.content: Because there are few cells, and they are still adjusting to the new conditions
options.rationale: Few cells are reproducing at first.

options.content: Because toxic ethanol has built up
options.rationale: Ethanol builds up later, in the stationary and death phases.

options.content: Because the death rate is higher than the birth rate when the yeast is first added
options.rationale: That happens in the death phase.

explanation: At the start there are only a few yeast cells, and they need time to adjust to the new conditions, for example by making the enzymes needed to use the sugar, before they reproduce quickly.
hints: What must the cells do before they can use the sugar?

stem: In a closed flask, a yeast population eventually decreases. Which is the best explanation?

options.content: Sugar runs out and toxic ethanol builds up, so more cells die than form.
options.rationale: The death rate exceeds the birth rate.

options.content: Yeast cells live for only a few minutes each.
options.rationale: The decline is caused by the conditions in the flask.

options.content: Predators enter the flask and eat the yeast.
options.rationale: The flask is closed.

options.content: The yeast cells all become dormant spores at the same time and stop dividing.
options.rationale: The fall is due to food shortage and toxic waste.

explanation: In a closed flask nothing new is added. The sugar runs out and ethanol accumulates to toxic levels, so the death rate becomes greater than the birth rate: the death phase.
hints: What is used up, and what builds up?

stem: What is meant by the **carrying capacity** of an environment?

options.content: The total mass of all the organisms in the environment
options.rationale: That is the biomass.

options.content: The number of different species living in the environment
options.rationale: That is a measure of biodiversity.

options.content: The largest population of a species the environment can support for long
options.rationale: It is set by limiting factors such as water and food.

options.content: The average amount of rain that the environment receives in one whole year
options.rationale: Rainfall affects carrying capacity but is not its definition.

explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population of a species that an environment can support for a long time, set by the resources in shortest supply.
hints: How many individuals can the area 'carry'?

stem: True or false: the carrying capacity of a grassland for zebra is the same every year.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not quite. Carrying capacity changes as resources change: after good rains more grass grows and more zebra can be supported; in a drought fewer.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Carrying capacity depends on resources such as food and water, which change from year to year.

explanation: Carrying capacity is set by limiting factors such as food and water. These vary with rainfall, so the carrying capacity of a grassland is higher in wet years than in droughts.
hints: Does the amount of grass stay the same every year?

stem:
Students grew yeast in a flask of sugar solution at 25 °C and counted the cells every 2 hours.

| Time / hours | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Yeast cells / millions per cm³ | 1.0 | 1.4 | 4.0 | 12.0 | 28.0 | 40.0 | 42.0 | 42.0 | 35.0 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which phase of growth is shown between 4 hours and 10 hours?

options.content: Lag phase
options.rationale: The lag phase is the slow start, from 0 to about 2 hours.

options.content: Exponential (log) phase
options.rationale: The numbers rise steeply, from 4.0 to 40.0 million per cm³.

options.content: Stationary (plateau) phase
options.rationale: The stationary phase is from about 12 to 14 hours.

options.content: Death phase
options.rationale: The numbers fall only after 14 hours.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean rate of increase in the number of yeast cells between 6 hours and 10 hours, in millions of cells per cm³ per hour.

payload.unitHint: million cells per cm³ per hour

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the number of yeast cells stayed the same between 12 and 14 hours.

points.description: Limiting factors: sugar (food) was running short / ethanol (toxic waste) was building up / competition for sugar
So the birth (reproduction) rate equalled the death rate

parts.explanation: By 12 hours the sugar was running short and ethanol, a toxic waste product, had built up. These limiting factors slowed reproduction and increased the death of cells until the birth rate equalled the death rate, so the number of cells stayed constant.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The students repeat the experiment with twice as much sugar in the same volume. Which result is most likely?

options.content: The yeast would never reach a stationary phase.
options.rationale: Sugar would still run out and ethanol still build up, only later.

options.content: The lag phase would disappear completely.
options.rationale: The cells still need time to adjust.

options.content: The maximum number of cells would be lower than before.
options.rationale: More food would support more cells, not fewer.

options.content: The population would reach a higher maximum, then level off.
options.rationale: More food raises the level at which limiting factors stop growth.

explanation: Between 4 and 10 hours the numbers rise steeply (exponential phase). From 6 to 10 hours they rise from 12.0 to 40.0 million per cm³, a mean rate of 28.0 ÷ 4 = 7 million per cm³ per hour. Later, limiting factors make the birth rate equal the death rate. More sugar would raise the maximum population.
workedSolution:
1. (a) Steep rise from 4 h to 10 h: exponential phase.
2. (b) Rate $= \dfrac{40.0 - 12.0}{10 - 6} = \dfrac{28.0}{4} = 7$ million cells per cm³ per hour.
3. (c) Sugar running short and ethanol building up; births = deaths.
4. (d) More food raises the maximum population (the carrying capacity of the flask).
hints: Rate = change in number ÷ change in time.

stem: In the dry season, most of the water in Hwange National Park comes from waterholes filled from boreholes. Large numbers of elephants gather around each waterhole.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which resource is most likely to limit the number of elephants an area can support in the dry season?

options.content: Water
options.rationale: There is little surface water, so elephants depend on the waterholes.

options.content: Oxygen
options.rationale: Oxygen is plentiful in the air.

options.content: Light
options.rationale: Light does not limit an elephant population.

options.content: Space to fly
options.rationale: Elephants do not fly.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe the effects on the ecosystem when the number of elephants near a waterhole exceeds the largest number that the area can support (its carrying capacity).

points.description: Vegetation is destroyed: trees are stripped of bark and branches, pushed over; grass is overgrazed
Other herbivores lose food / shelter, so their numbers fall; biodiversity falls
Bare ground is trampled and eroded (degradation)
Crowding spreads disease, and animals die of hunger in droughts

parts.explanation: When there are too many elephants, they strip the bark and branches of trees, push trees over and overgraze the grass. Other herbivores lose their food and shelter, so their numbers fall. The ground is trampled bare and the soil erodes. Crowding also helps disease to spread, and in drought years many animals die of hunger.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which management action would spread the elephants over a larger area and reduce the damage around each waterhole?

options.content: Closing most of the waterholes so that elephants crowd at the few that are left
options.rationale: This would concentrate the elephants even more.

options.content: Pumping water into more waterholes spread across the park
options.rationale: Elephants would then use a larger area of vegetation.

options.content: Fencing all the elephants into one small area
options.rationale: This would increase the damage in that area.

options.content: Removing all the trees near the waterholes
options.rationale: This would destroy the habitat completely.

explanation: In the dry season water is the main limiting factor, so elephants crowd at waterholes. Exceeding the carrying capacity leads to habitat damage, food shortage for other species, erosion, disease and deaths. Spreading water across the park spreads the elephants out.
workedSolution:
1. (a) Water is scarce in the dry season.
2. (b) Overbrowsing and overgrazing, loss of food and shelter for other species, trampling and erosion, disease and starvation.
3. (c) More waterholes spread the elephants over more vegetation.
hints: Which resource is scarcest in the dry season?

stem: Why does a population of bacteria in fresh nutrient broth grow exponentially for a time?

options.content: Because the bacteria are dying faster than they are able to divide
options.rationale: That would make the population fall.

options.content: Because toxic wastes have built up in the broth
options.rationale: Toxic wastes slow growth.

options.content: Because food and space are plentiful, so births far exceed deaths
options.rationale: No factor is limiting yet.

options.content: Because the bacteria have stopped reproducing altogether
options.rationale: Then the population could not grow.

explanation: With plenty of nutrients and space, little competition and few wastes, nothing limits reproduction. Each bacterium divides regularly, so the population doubles again and again.
hints: Is anything in short supply at this stage?

stem: At the start of a year, a game reserve had 1200 impala. During the year, 300 impala were born, 180 died and 20 moved out of the reserve. None moved in. How many impala were there at the end of the year?
explanation: Final number $= 1200 + 300 - 180 - 20 = 1300$ impala.
workedSolution:
1. Add the births: 1200 + 300 = 1500.
2. Subtract the deaths: 1500 − 180 = 1320.
3. Subtract those that moved out: 1320 − 20 = 1300.
hints: Births add to a population; deaths and animals leaving reduce it.

stem: A few bacteria are added to a closed flask of nutrient broth. Describe and explain the shape of the population growth curve that would be obtained over several days. [6]

points.description: Lag phase: slow increase at first
because there are few bacteria and they are adjusting / making enzymes
Exponential (log) phase: rapid increase, doubling at regular intervals, because there are plenty of nutrients and space; births far exceed deaths
because limiting factors (nutrients running short, toxic waste building up, competition) make the birth rate equal the death rate
Death phase: numbers fall because nutrients run out and wastes become toxic, so the death rate exceeds the birth rate

answerSpec.modelAnswer: At first the population increases slowly: this is the lag phase. There are only a few bacteria and they are adjusting to the broth, for example by making the enzymes they need. Next comes the exponential (log) phase: there are plenty of nutrients and space and few wastes, so the birth rate is far greater than the death rate and the population doubles at regular intervals. Then the curve levels off in the stationary phase: nutrients start to run short, toxic wastes build up and there is competition, so the birth rate falls until it equals the death rate. Finally, in the death phase, the nutrients run out and the wastes become toxic, so the death rate is greater than the birth rate and the numbers fall.

explanation: A sigmoid curve has lag, exponential, stationary and death phases, explained by the balance between births and deaths as limiting factors take effect.
hints: Describe each phase, then explain it in terms of births, deaths and limiting factors.

stem: Which factor is most likely to limit the population of fish in a small, warm pond that is overgrown with decaying plants?

options.content: The amount of light reaching the fish
options.rationale: Fish do not need light to survive.

options.content: The amount of nitrogen gas in the air
options.rationale: Fish do not use nitrogen gas.

options.content: The number of fishermen who visit the pond each week
options.rationale: Nothing in the description suggests fishing.

options.content: The concentration of dissolved oxygen in the water
options.rationale: Decomposers use oxygen, and warm water holds less of it.

explanation: Decomposers breaking down the dead plants use up dissolved oxygen, and warm water holds less oxygen than cool water. Fish need dissolved oxygen, so it is likely to be the limiting factor.
hints: What do decomposers use as they respire?

stem: Select **all** the factors that can limit the growth of a population.

options.content: Competition for space
options.rationale: Lack of space limits feeding and breeding.

options.content: Disease
options.rationale: Disease spreads quickly in crowded populations.

options.content: The absence of predators
options.rationale: No predators means less is limiting the population.

options.content: An unlimited supply of water
options.rationale: Plenty of water allows growth; it does not limit it.

options.content: Predation
options.rationale: Predators kill members of the population.

options.content: A shortage of food
options.rationale: Less food means fewer young are produced and survive.

options.content: Plenty of nesting sites
options.rationale: A good supply of nesting sites helps the population grow.

explanation: Food shortage, predation, disease and competition for resources such as space all limit population growth. Plentiful resources and the absence of predators allow a population to grow.
hints: A limiting factor is something in short supply or something that kills.

stem: What term describes all the populations of different species living together in an ecosystem?

rejected.feedback: A population is one species. All the species together form a community.
An ecosystem includes the physical environment as well. The living populations together are the community.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives.

explanation: All the populations of different species in an ecosystem make up the community. The community and its physical environment together form the ecosystem.
hints: It is the word used for a group of people living in one place, too.

stem: After good rains, a population of red locusts in a grassland increases very rapidly. A few weeks later, the population falls sharply. Which is the most likely explanation for the fall?

options.content: They ate most of the food, so food became limiting and many died or left.
options.rationale: Rapid growth used up the resource that allowed it.

options.content: The locusts' birth rate became much greater than their death rate.
options.rationale: That would make the population rise.

options.content: The good rains increased the food supply for them even more.
options.rationale: More food would not cause a crash.

options.content: Locusts cannot reproduce in grassland.
options.rationale: They reproduced rapidly at first, so they can.

explanation: With plenty of food after the rains, the locusts multiplied rapidly. They soon ate most of the grass, so food became limiting: the death rate rose above the birth rate (and many locusts moved away), so the population crashed.
hints: What happens to the food when a population grows very fast?
